The Boston Patriots officially became the New England Patriots on March 22, 1971 [d2][d4][d8]. The name change came as the team relocated to a new stadium in Foxborough, Massachusetts, and the original proposed name "Bay State Patriots" was rejected by the NFL [d2][d4]. According to team owner Billy Sullivan, "The feeling now is that the Patriots are representing all New England, not just the city of Boston, not just the state of Massachusetts" [d8]. Prior to 1971, the team had played as the Boston Patriots since their founding in 1960 as a charter member of the AFL [d6][d9].
